assessment.governing_intent: Produce a Wave 2A integration/capstone proof for already-proven upstream capabilities. The capabilities are, in order: inventory, ambiguity, premise/proof, independent design applicability, compiler-derived initial compilation, and lint/retained Agent Ready assessment consumption. The proof must show that a source, decision or design revision mismatch holds downstream readiness without mutating lifecycle or Project state, and that no output asserts release.
implementation_unknowns: Whether the existing tests under tests/context_assembly and src/alienintent/composition/upstream_profile.py already cover the chained end-to-end path, or need an integration harness added over FX-A.
How to inject a source, decision or design revision mutation into FX-A so it discriminates stale-evidence reuse without touching lifecycle or Project state.
How to observe that no lifecycle or Project mutation occurred, for example through an outside-state readback, using existing OperationalStore/EvidenceRepository boundaries.
Which of the four material failure classes the existing tests already exercise as discriminating negative controls, and which need exactly one new control each.
Whether the retained Agent Ready consumption boundary from WO-220209 exposes a stable typed interface the integration can consume without copying the rubric.
The exact interface and output identity of the WO-220208 compiler once it is materialized, needed to bind compilation into the chain and record producer/version provenance.
material_risks: Proceeding before WO-220208 materializes invites emulating or stubbing the compiler inside the capstone. That violates the non-goals and Reuse Before Build, and it would produce proof that does not reflect the real producer.
A green local result could be misread as release or execution admission, despite the explicit non-claims.
Stale evidence reuse across revisions if revision pins (fixture, source, profile, candidate) are not captured exactly.
Implementation-location paths (context_assembly, legacy bounded_context) could be treated as semantic ownership decisions. The task says FD-02 refinement leaves that mapping undecided.
Shape-matching Agent Ready output could be mistaken for producer provenance. Producer identity and version must be checked independently.
Fixed decisions are duplicated verbatim in the task text. This is harmless now but indicates compilation noise that could hide a real divergence in later revisions.
assessment.next_action: Hold this BIU until WO-220208 is materialized, proven and DONE, with its candidate SHA and producer/version provenance recorded. Then confirm WO-220209's DONE evidence, and request a fresh native Agent Ready assessment of the exact revision before assigning the PRODUCER.
assessment.rationale: Governing intent is clear and the owner decisions this node needs are recorded as settled. Allocation, edge policy, Agent Ready ownership and the dispositions are fixed. The FD-02 mapping is explicitly outside this node, so CLARIFY is not warranted. The work is a single cohesive integration concern with one fixture and one verdict, so SPLIT would be artificial decomposition. The controlling condition is an unavailable external prerequisite. The task text reports WO-220208 as UNMATERIALIZED, yet its output (compiler-derived initial compilation) is an integral stage of the chain being integrated. The task forbids implementing or repairing upstream capabilities here and requires all predecessors to be DONE. That is a HOLD on a missing artifact, not unresolved intent. Once WO-220208 is available, the remaining unknowns are engineering research and the task would likely qualify as READY.
assessment.summary: Intent, scope, non-goals, fixed decisions and proof policy are coherent and detailed. The work is one integration concern with a single fixture (FX-A), named existing proof surfaces and an initial bounded command. The controlling problem is a missing prerequisite rather than unclear intent. The task text reports that dependency WO-220208 is UNMATERIALIZED. WO-220208 is the compiler-derived initial BiuContract compilation under the SF-REQ-013 amendment, and it is one of the stages this capstone must integrate. The task's own non-goals forbid building or repairing that capability inside the capstone, and its readiness section requires every predecessor BIU to be DONE. WO-220209 is reported DONE (Issue #105); this gate has not independently verified that.
assessment.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable and supports one meaningful independent verdict. The verifier can check that the chained stages run in order on FX-A, and that each failure class (ordering gate, revision-mismatch invalidation, typed separation of compilation from assessment consumption, no mutation or release assertion) has a discriminating negative control. The verifier can also check that outside-state readback is unchanged and that evidence and provenance receipts are retained. Custody (exact SHA, fresh verifier worktree) is well specified. However, the compiler-derived initial compilation stage cannot be observed until WO-220208 exists. Any verdict produced now would either be incomplete or rely on a stub, and the task forbids a stub as a substitute for the provider.
